Outbreak of Legionnaires’ Disease Hits Austrian Electric Utilities Industry

Vienna, June 14—An outbreak of Legionnaires’ disease has affected the workforce of several electric utilities across Austria, prompting concerns over worker safety and operational continuity, industry officials said Friday.

The outbreak, first identified last week at a regional power plant operated by Alpenkraft Energie AG in Upper Austria, has since been confirmed at three additional sites run by separate companies in Lower Austria and Styria. Company representatives reported that at least 37 employees have tested positive for the bacterial infection, which is believed to have originated from contaminated cooling towers at affected facilities.

“We are working closely with health authorities to identify the source and implement immediate decontamination protocols,” said Elisabeth Gruber, spokesperson for Alpenkraft Energie AG. “Our priority remains the health of our workers and the safe operation of our site.”

The Austrian Electric Utilities Association (AEUA) stated in a release that precautionary inspections and testing of water systems have been expanded to all member companies. “We urge all operators to review their maintenance protocols and take preventive action,” said AEUA president Markus Lechner. “The safety of our staff is paramount, and we are coordinating closely to minimize further cases.”

Several affected plants have reduced non-essential on-site staffing as a precaution, and shifts have been adjusted to limit employee contact. At least five workers from the initial cluster remain hospitalized, though no fatalities have been reported as of Friday afternoon.

Union representatives have raised concerns about the adequacy of existing safety protocols. “We have long called for more rigorous monitoring of cooling systems, especially during seasonal maintenance,” said Veronika Stein, regional chair of the Utilities Workers Union. “We expect a thorough review and concrete improvements.”

Austrian health authorities are investigating the outbreak in partnership with the utilities and have recommended immediate risk assessments at all industry sites. The situation remains fluid as further testing continues. Industry officials expect some disruption to ongoing projects and routine operations until the outbreak is contained.

“We are taking every possible measure to protect our teams,” Gruber said.
